answer: To resist sybils, agents must grow a continuous vine of attested interactions on a shared dune of reputation before gaining full market access. Each new identity begins with zero throughput and earns capacity only as peers confirm real work, binding it to a unique opal-like cryptographic commitment that cannot be cheaply cloned. An attacker funding N fakes must wait through the slow growth period for every one and pay the opportunity cost of idle capital, making mass creation uneconomic compared to honest participation.
